# Independent sealed cold-prefix review

Reviewed frozen manifest `4a0900cb3f21436ab882c6d3f3206489e003813d204746469447ffb3717e8cd2`. No concrete production defect found in this bounded inspection. Two additional actual-Core regressions are supplied for uncovered cases; they have not been compiled or executed by this reviewer.

The public `reexecute_historical_rows` wrapper (reference replay lines 41–69) passes `&expected.current` as the common body's actual Post. Thus the public exact-current contract does not acquire the carrier's later-Post admission. The common body still independently checks the original archive endpoint/physical entries, raw origin and source row receipt. The extra historical-tip read happens before constructing finance. `check.py` derives the entire common body from committed `bad3892` using the frozen transform; Rust 1.90 formatting produces the frozen reference exactly. All 12 frozen payload hashes were verified.

The common body constructs one Replay from raw foundation commands (line 116), calls the original historical RowPC loop and checks actual playback completion before its one effects drain (line 219). It keeps original source results, validity, effects and before/after records. The receipt is pushed into the actual retained prefix before recorded-byte comparison (lines 245–246); a mismatch returns that financial owner, index and actual prefix, rather than a valid Session/head. No supplied financial state or recorded result is used to execute the source.

The carrier acquires the real final-Post capability first (carrier line 88) and retains it on common-body failure (line 118). Its public accessors expose immutable diagnostics and explicitly historical prefix receipts/head, plus separate completed-tip and actual-Post pins. It adds no mutable financial/index access, ordinary Session conversion, Replay release, checkpoint or capability-release method. Rejected state retains the same index lock. This establishes API/ownership scope by inspection, not chain authentication or complete service recovery.

Parent's initial two failing carrier controls were input assertions, not evidence of a production guard gap: importing the already existing raw ID after its actual validity update conflicts before put and must preserve original `WrongContext`. A fresh raw ID reaches the guarded put and must return `ColdWriteRefused`. The reviewer accepts Parent's test-only correction; neither production import order nor admission should change.

The three original carrier tests cover an empty completed prefix/empty native history before a later genuine write and a pre-financial historical-pin rejection. The proposed additive tests strengthen two distinct boundaries:

1. Execute an actual nonempty raw Main row/validity write, archive it, then execute a different raw row to obtain a later genuine native Post. Rebuild the earlier financial prefix while retaining that later native owner, unchanged IO counters and exclusive lock; the old public API must still reject it before finance.
2. Alter a recorded logical receipt, repair only its envelope CRC/archive digest, and retain the original independent head/foundation/physical pins. Actual source reconstruction must occur, then comparison must reject while retaining its actual effects/financial prefix, final-Post capability and lock. A fresh raw input proves guarded put refusal without the existing-ID conflict.

Only raw origin metadata is inserted before adoption. Later metadata/financial changes come from original source execution. No test backend imports source outcomes or financial snapshots. The two new tests use real private production types and existing real fixture helpers; no stub adapter was run. Their Rust syntax was parsed/formatted with Rust 1.90, but Parent must run the actual Core tests.

Remaining scope: this carrier is not full acknowledged catchup/service/action reexecution, mutation recovery, an unlocked live owner, or a proof of Windows power-loss durability. Historical generation availability and independently retained original pins remain required. Source/type errors and native local refusals continue through the existing execution body; the new carrier does not repair them.
RootTestSyntaxCorrection: Use matches! for exact ColdWriteRefused in two new independent cold-prefix controls; production error type remains unchanged and expected refusal variant is identical.
